entries.name: Saiga antelope
entries.migrates: great annual migrations between winter and summer pasture
behaviour: bulbous proboscis filters dust and warms freezing air
mass gatherings in spring give birth synchronously
vast migratory columns cross the open steppe
entries.notes: The icon of the Eurasian steppe: the strange downward-facing nose filters dust and cold. Recovered from near-collapse by poaching; herds of over a million were counted again in Kazakhstan.

entries.name: Przewalski's horse
entries.migrates: seasonal short-distance wandering between pastures
behaviour: small harems: one stallion, several mares and their young
stiff upright mane and dun coat with a dark dorsal stripe
known in Mongolia as the takhi, a spirit-animal of the steppe
entries.notes: The last truly wild horse on Earth; extinct in the wild until reintroduction to Mongolia in the 1990s. Model the stocky dun build and the short, standing mane.

entries.name: Kulan (Asiatic wild ass)
entries.migrates: seasonal routes to water and spring pasture
behaviour: separate stallion harems and bachelor bands
very fast across hardpan and gravel plains
extremely wary of humans; a quarry of desert kings

voxel_model.pattern: sandy back, white belly, dark dorsal stripe

entries.notes: The onager of the old steppes and deserts; a prized royal hunt. Its range is now relics in Iran, Central Asia and India's Little Rann of Kutch.

entries.name: Goitered gazelle
entries.migrates: seasonal latitudinal and altitudinal shifts
behaviour: black tail and sandy coat blend into gravel plains
rutting males develop a goiter-like throat swelling
runs in a straight line, never bounding like African gazelles
entries.notes: Vulnerable across a shrinking range; desert kites in the Neolithic mass-killed its ancestors by the tens of thousands. The goiter shows only in the winter rut.

entries.name: Mongolian gazelle
entries.migrates: spring and autumn migrations; routes vary with weather and forage
behaviour: heart-shaped white rump patch
winter aggregations of many thousands; mega-herds into the hundred-thousands
rutting males grow a goiter-like throat swelling

voxel_model.pattern: tawny with heart-shaped white rump patch

entries.notes: Roughly 1.5 million survive across Mongolia and adjacent China; a quarter-million were counted in a single 2007 mega-herd. Gestation is about 5 to 6 months, unusually long for a gazelle.

entries.name: American bison
entries.migrates: seasonal movements between summer and winter range
behaviour: bulls battle wreathing in dust wallows
shaggy hump of shoulders acts as a battering ram
herds can change the state of the prairie they graze
entries.notes: The monument-animal of the North American grassland; nearly annihilated by slaughter, now back in managed herds. Its grazing, like fire, maintains the prairie.

entries.name: Pronghorn
entries.migrates: long seasonal migrations between summer and winter ranges
behaviour: fastest sustained runner in North America, built for the long chase
stands on rises to scan the open grass
black horns branch to form forward and backward hooks

voxel_model.pattern: tan with white rump and black prongs

entries.notes: Neither antelope nor deer — the last living member of its own family, over-built for speed against predators that no longer exist. Twins are the rule.

entries.name: Wild Bactrian camel
entries.migrates: wanders between water holes and forage grounds
behaviour: two humps rather than the dromedary's one
double wool coat survives winters at -40°C
salt-lick desert oases still harbour its last wild herds
entries.notes: Critically endangered, with fewer than about a thousand left in the Lop Nur and Gobi salt deserts. One of Earth's last undiscovered megafauna until the 20th century.

entries.name: Grey wolf
entries.migrates: follows the great ungulate ranges
behaviour: howl carries for kilometres and pins down territory
family packs hunt saiga and horses cooperatively
the reason open-country ungulates run so fast
entries.notes: The steppe apex predator; bison, saiga and horses evolved their vigilance against it. Packs may range hundreds of kilometres in a year.

entries.name: Coyote
behaviour: pairs hunt cooperatively at night
yip-howls in chorus across open country
the trickster-generalist that fills every gap
entries.notes: The North American grassland's chorus at dusk; a generalist that thrives on roadkill, rodents and near-extinction-proof adaptability.

entries.name: Great bustard
entries.migrates: seasonal migration across open country
behaviour: heaviest flying bird alive; males push 16 kg
males inflate balloon-display with white underplumage
ground nests vanish in tall grass
entries.notes: The world's heaviest flying bird; its boom carries kilometres and the balloon display is pure theatre. gestation_days is incubation time.

entries.name: Golden eagle
entries.migrates: partial migrant; wanders widely in winter
behaviour: stoops on prey from cliff ledges at great speed
the berkutchi of Kazakh falconry — tamed to hunt fox and hare on horseback
golden nape feathers backlit in sunlight
entries.notes: The Kazakh berkutchi fly golden eagles against fox and saiga on horseback — a falconry tradition thousands of years old. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Steppe eagle
entries.migrates: long migration to southern wintering grounds
behaviour: hangs low over ground-squirrel colonies scanning for prey
gathers in numbers around carcasses and pellets
near threatened; nests on cliffs and pylons
entries.notes: The dark eagle of the steppe; the raptor to model soaring over taverns of marmots. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Eastern imperial eagle
entries.migrates: partial migration to milder winter quarters
behaviour: hunts from high soaring, dropping on ground rodents
adults carry white shoulder epaulets
nests in isolated old trees at field and steppe edges
entries.notes: The white epaulets are the mark to carry into the voxel model; vulnerable across its range. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Saker falcon
entries.migrates: short-distance migrations to milder ranges
behaviour: stoop of well over 200 km/h is the hunting signature
nests on cliff ledges and electricity pylons
trapped heavily for falconry, driving declines
entries.notes: The falconers' bird for two thousand years; a working hunting raptor, not just a wild animal. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Demoiselle crane
entries.migrates: long-distance migration to wintering grounds in India and Africa
behaviour: white neck plumes stream behind in flight
staging flocks of hundreds gather before departure
elaborate courtship leaps and dances

voxel_model.pattern: slate grey with white neck plumes

entries.notes: Tens of thousands stream over the Himalayas each autumn between Mongolia and India. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: European roller
entries.migrates: migrates to sub-Saharan Africa for winter
behaviour: turquoise-and-chestnut flash when it leaves a perch
tumbles and rolls in courtship flights
nests in river-side hollow trees
entries.notes: The most saturated colour on the steppe; nests in old trees along steppe watercourses. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Greater rhea
behaviour: male incubates communal nests alone for over a month
zig-zag escape runs with raised flapping wings
open pampas grassland specialist; scattered by farmland
entries.notes: The pampas ostrich; a male can hatch twenty chicks from one communal scrape with the whole harem contributing eggs. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Grey partridge
behaviour: winter coveys of a dozen birds walking fields
explosive flush flight when flushed
declined sharply with pesticide-era farming

voxel_model.pattern: grey body, chestnut face, barred flanks

entries.notes: The 'hungarian partridge' of game coverts; a ground-nesting steppe bird that vanished almost entirely from farmed Europe. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Black-bellied sandgrouse
entries.migrates: local daily movements to drinking water
behaviour: flies tens of kilometres at dawn and dusk to drink
brood male soaks belly feathers to carry water to chicks
lays on bare stony ground with no cover
entries.notes: Sandgrouse must drink every day; hundreds streaming to a single water at dawn is a scene worth scripting. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Eurasian skylark
entries.migrates: partial migration to milder winter quarters
behaviour: sings in a climbing, hovering display flight high above the fields
invisible against the turf until it flushes
a warble that defines open-country morning
entries.notes: The soundtrack of the steppe morning; the song is what matters, not the visual model.

entries.name: Corsac fox
entries.migrates: wanders widely in search of water and prey
behaviour: a tireless trotter with exceptional endurance
digs dens in loose soil, often sharing burrows with badgers
hunted across the steppe for its pelt for centuries
entries.notes: A long-distance trotter among foxes; its burrows are ready-made shelter for other species on the steppe.

entries.name: Pallas's cat
behaviour: flat broad head and huge plush double coat — the 'steppe owl-cat'
waits motionless among rocks for hours
funny-faced living fossil of the cold steppe

voxel_model.pattern: grey-brown with dark spots and white cheek ruffs

entries.notes: The manul; sits motionless in a rock field and lets danger assume it is a stone. The single most charismatic cat of the cold steppe.

entries.name: Eversmann's polecat (steppe polecat)
behaviour: caches surplus prey in underground larders
fierce to devoted defending kits in the burrow
bold enough to chase animals many times its size

voxel_model.pattern: dark mask and legs, pale body

entries.notes: The fear racing through the rodent warrens at night; outkills and outwits animals far larger than itself.

entries.name: Bobak marmot
behaviour: sits upright over its burrow as a sentry, whistling alarm
hibernates 6 to 8 months of the year underground
colonial warrens stud the Ukrainian and Russian black-soil steppe
entries.notes: The upright sentry of the black-soil steppe; its whistle is the proverbial alarm of the grasslands.

entries.name: Mongolian marmot (tarbagan)
behaviour: colonial burrowers; whistling sentries over steppe holes
hibernation nearly half the year underground
a historic reservoir of plague in Central Asia
entries.notes: The tarbagan; a Mongolian staple of fur and meat and the animal tied to plague's history on the steppe.

entries.name: Black-tailed prairie dog
behaviour: towns can span hundreds of square kilometres
barking and chirping sentry calls across a colony
unearthed the soil itself — the 'dog' is outsized by its digging
entries.notes: The town-builder: prairie dogs shaped the American grassland soil and fed black-footed ferrets and bison herds around them.

entries.name: Long-tailed ground squirrel
behaviour: colonial burrower of river meadows at the steppe edge
8-month hibernation shrinks its active year
runs in squeaking speckled streams along roads and railways
entries.notes: The speckled river-meadow ground squirrel; a writhing carpet of little bodies along every ditch in the steppe margin.

entries.name: European (common) hamster
behaviour: cheek pouches haul grain into underground larders
attacks much larger animals when cornered
true hibernator; caches 10 kg of grain per burrow

voxel_model.pattern: orange back, black belly, white mid-flanks

entries.notes: The great granary-rodent; farmer-exterminated across Europe for stripping crops before combines can.

entries.name: European hare
behaviour: lies up by day in a scratched 'form'
superfetation: a doe can carry two litters at once
zig-zag bolting flight and startling 'boxing' matches
entries.notes: The brown hare of open farms; its leverets are born eyes-open in the grass — no nest at all.

entries.name: Black-tailed jackrabbit
behaviour: huge black-tipped ears swivel to track danger
flashes a black-tipped tail and rump in flight
bounds in long loping gallops across open ground
entries.notes: A hare, not a rabbit; the classic darting silhouette of the open American West.

entries.name: Great jerboa
behaviour: bipedal hopping like a miniature kangaroo
long tuft-tipped tail balances the hops
hibernates deep underground half the year
entries.notes: The steppe's tiny biped; half its year is spent dormant, the rest is explosive hopping by night.

entries.name: Horsfield's tortoise
behaviour: four toes on the front feet (unlike most tortoises' five)
hibernates 6 to 8 months in clay burrows
males fight with head-butting and shell-ramming
entries.notes: The Russian tortoise; digs burrows deeper than half a metre and sleeps through the -40 winters. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Steppe viper
behaviour: gives birth to live young in summer
cryptic on trampled game trails and salt pans
mild, rarely dangerous venom; shy and secretive
entries.notes: The signature steppe snake; thousands of tiny diamonds underfoot on the grazing runs. gestation_days is the live-birth carry.

entries.name: Italian locust
entries.migrates: outbreak swarms march and fly to fresh pasture
behaviour: outbreak years strip crops and steppe turf overnight
hindwings flash brick-red in flight
one generation per year; eggs overwinter in soil
entries.notes: The 'locust' of steppe plague years; model it as weather as much as as creature.
